title: Putin's Iran diplomacy faces limits as Russia eyes Ukraine concessions
gist: Al-Monitor analysis: Russia is stepping up Iran-US mediation, including a proposal to take Iran's roughly 440 kg of 60% enriched uranium, hoping to earn leverage with Trump on Ukraine despite limited influence in Tehran.

insights.claim: Russia is pushing mediation between the US and Iran in the hope Trump will reward it with concessions on Ukraine, despite limited influence on Tehran.
insights.speaker: Anton Mardasov
insights.so_what: Iran diplomacy and the Ukraine settlement are linked in Moscow's strategy.

insights.claim: Moscow proposed transferring roughly 440 kg of Iranian uranium enriched to 60% to Russia, but Tehran refuses to ship its stockpiles abroad, viewing them as a deterrent.
insights.speaker: Anton Mardasov
insights.so_what: The main diplomatic off-ramp is blocked by Iran's deterrence logic.
insights.locator: Moscow also proposed a specific mechanism

insights.claim: Russian diplomatic sources say the uranium-transfer proposal is practically the only card Moscow has to play.
insights.speaker: Anton Mardasov
insights.so_what: Russia's leverage is thin; mediation success odds are low.
insights.locator: Sources in the Russian diplomatic corps

insights.claim: Putin received Trump envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21, discussing Ukraine and saying Iran diplomatic options were not exhausted.
insights.speaker: Anton Mardasov
insights.so_what: Russia-US channel is live on both files.

insights.claim: The IRGC has threatened to invade any Middle Eastern neighbor that supports a US campaign, amid reports of preparations for a new US military operation, shifting momentum back toward confrontation.
insights.speaker: Anton Mardasov
insights.so_what: Renewed US-Iran military action risk remains elevated despite parallel diplomacy.
